# claude-toolkit

Personal Claude Code plugins, laid out as a private plugin marketplace. A proof of concept: it is compatible with the team-shared SDD skill but entirely separate from it, and never changes it. Every toolkit agent carries the `toolkit:` prefix.

## What it does

Open a project in VS Code and a **coordinator** Claude session starts in an editor tab. It reports the SDD team recap, reads the project board and asks what is next. You tell it the goal; it creates the **worker** sessions the job needs, each in its own named tab with a written brief, and follows them through SendMessage. Workers that still have open work reopen with their conversation the next time you open the project. You can still type in any worker's tab.

| Part | Where |
|---|---|
| `toolkit:coordinator` and `toolkit:worker` agents | `plugins/toolkit/agents/` |
| Start-up hook: runs SDD's team-mailbox pull for the coordinator only | `plugins/toolkit/hooks/` |
| VS Code extension: starts the coordinator, reopens active workers, opens requested workers | `vscode/` |

One project at a time; coordinating several projects is planned.

## Set up (once per machine)

Link the extension into VS Code, then reload VS Code (Command Palette → "Developer: Reload Window"):

```
New-Item -ItemType Junction -Path "$env:USERPROFILE\.vscode\extensions\dserri.claude-toolkit-0.0.1" -Target "<clone>\vscode"
```

The extension starts every session with `--plugin-dir <clone>/plugins/toolkit` and `--permission-mode auto` (sessions in the same mode exchange messages without approval prompts). `claude` must be on `PATH`, or set `claudeToolkit.claudePath`; `claudeToolkit.pluginDir` overrides the plugin folder. `claudeToolkit.workerLayout` chooses where worker tabs open: `beside` (default, the column next to the coordinator) or `tabs` (full-width tabs in the coordinator's column).

## Enable a project

Open the project folder and run "Toolkit: Enable coordinator in this folder". It records the folder as enabled on this machine (in the extension's own storage, never in the repository), creates `.coord/`, adds it to `.git/info/exclude` (never `.gitignore`), and opens the coordinator. From then on the coordinator opens whenever VS Code opens the folder; "Toolkit: Start coordinator" opens it again if you closed it. A repository that carries a `.coord/` folder starts nothing until you enable it yourself, and the extension's settings are machine-scoped, so a workspace cannot change which executable or plugin it runs.

### The board (`.coord/`)

| File | Written by | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `team.json` | coordinator | `[{ "name", "role", "state": "active" \| "done" }]`; active workers reopen at start-up |
| `workers/<name>/brief.md` | coordinator | the worker's task |
| `workers/<name>/status.md` | worker | `State`, `Summary`, `Next` |
| `requests/<name>.json` | coordinator | `{ "name": "<name>" }`: asks the extension to open the worker; rejected requests leave `<name>.rejected.md` |
| `log.md` | coordinator | decisions, assignments and outcomes |
| `sessions/<session name>.id` | start-up hook | each worker's session ID, so its tab resumes exactly its own conversation, also when the coordinator requests a finished worker again |

Sessions are named `<project>-coordinator` and `<project>-<worker>` (the project folder name in lowercase, other characters as hyphens); tabs show the short name. Enabled projects need different folder names, or their sessions share names.

## Session status

The "Claude sessions" view (its own icon in the Activity Bar, the same in every window; drag it elsewhere once if you prefer) and the status-bar item show every interactive Claude Code session on this machine, toolkit or not. Clicking the status-bar item (`🔔 2 waiting`) shows the session waiting longest; `Ctrl+Alt+N` ("Toolkit: Next waiting session") cycles through the waiting sessions in urgency order; both reach tabs in other windows like a card click does.

| Colour | Status | Set by |
|---|---|---|
| red | waiting for permission / waiting for your answer | `PermissionRequest`; `AskUserQuestion`, or a turn ending with `STATUS: QUESTION` (coordinator and worker) or a final `?` |
| purple | possibly stuck | working with no event for `claudeToolkit.stuckMinutes` (default 10) |
| yellow | finished, needs review | any other end of turn |
| green | working | a prompt or a tool result |
| grey | idle | session started, no prompt yet |

Cards are grouped by project folder (the most urgent project first; each group shows how many of its sessions wait) and sorted by urgency inside each group (longest waiting first) and show the time in that status, the last tool used ("after Bash"; only finished tool calls are recorded) or the tool asking for permission, and the last line of the last message. Click a card to focus its tab, in any VS Code window: each window lists the session tabs it opened in `~/.agent-status/windows/<pid>.json`, and a click on a session held by another window brings that window to the front (by opening its folder) and asks it, through `~/.agent-status/focus/<pid>.json`, to show the tab. A card's tooltip says where its session runs; a session started by hand outside the toolkit's tabs only gets a message. Hide a card with its eye icon until the session's next event. Closing a tab hides its card.

Install the hooks once (they back up `~/.claude/settings.json` first and add only their own entries):

```
node <clone>/status/install.mjs
node <clone>/status/install.mjs --uninstall
```

The hook (`status/status-hook.mjs`) runs asynchronously, so sessions never wait for it, and appends one line per event to `~/.agent-status/sessions/<session_id>.jsonl`; errors go to `~/.agent-status/hook.log`. It deletes a session's file at `SessionEnd` and leaves a `<session_id>.ended` marker so late background events cannot bring the session back (a new start or resume clears it), and, when a session starts, removes files and markers idle for more than 6 hours (`STALE_HOURS` at the top of the script). Headless sessions (`claude -p`, SDK, SDD's reviewer) are skipped by the observed but undocumented `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=sdk-*` value; `tests/status-entrypoint.e2e.mjs` checks it against the installed CLI. A denied permission stays red until the turn ends, because Claude Code fires no event for a denial.

## Plugin delivery

The organization's managed Claude Code policy currently allows only the official Anthropic marketplace, so the plugin is loaded from the clone with `--plugin-dir` (the extension does it; by hand: `claude --plugin-dir <clone>/plugins/toolkit`). Update with `git pull`, then reload VS Code.

Once an admin allows the marketplace:

```
claude plugin marketplace add dserri/claude-toolkit
claude plugin install toolkit@claude-toolkit
```

and enable auto-update for `claude-toolkit` in `/plugin` → Marketplaces. The plugin declares no version, so every pushed commit is a release.

## Roll back

Delete the `dserri.claude-toolkit-0.0.1` junction and reload VS Code; remove a project's `.coord/` folder if you no longer want its board. Sessions started by hand work as before.

## Develop

```
node --test
node --test tests/coordinator.e2e.mjs tests/status-entrypoint.e2e.mjs
```

The first runs the unit, hook, installer and `claude plugin validate` tests (`claude` must be on `PATH`). The second starts real headless sessions with a model call. Tab behaviour and the session view in VS Code are verified by hand.

# Design

## Context

See proposal.md. The view, the click routing (own tab, other window via registry and focus request, or message) and urgency sorting already exist. VS Code stores Explorer view placement and sizes per workspace, which is why the view shifts between windows; an Activity Bar container is a fixed home the developer can still drag elsewhere once.

## Goals / Non-Goals

**Goals:** one click or key to the waiting session; same view placement everywhere; optional full-width workers.

**Non-Goals:** notifications (later, only if red cards are missed); the coordinator reading the status files (later); the supervisor.

## Decisions

- **One focus path.** The status-bar command and the next-waiting command reuse the card click (`focus(session)`), so every route reaches other windows the same way.
- **Pure selection in `status-core.js`:** `waitingSessions(sessions)` (waiting ones in urgency order) and `nextWaiting(waiting, lastFocusedId)` (the one after the last focused, wrapping, first when unknown). The view remembers the last focused session id in memory.
- **Activity Bar container** `claudeToolkit` with an SVG icon in `vscode/media/`, holding the `claudeToolkit.sessions` view; the status-bar fallback runs `claudeToolkit.sessions.focus`.
- **Shortcut** `ctrl+alt+n` (no conflict on this machine; developers can rebind it).
- **Worker layout** read when a tab opens; `terminalOptions` takes the tab's `role` (`coordinator` or `worker`) and the `layout` instead of the `beside` flag, so core stays the single place deciding placement: coordinator in column 1 with focus, workers in column 2 (or column 1 with `tabs`) without taking focus.
- **Registry files written atomically** (found in review): readers delete unreadable window files, so each window writes its own file through a temporary file and rename, like focus requests. Reading and writing live in `vscode/registry.js`, plain Node, tested directly.
- **Follow-ups:** registry reader deletes by the file name it read (unreadable files included); focus requests written as temp file plus rename; routing decisions moved into a pure `clickAction(location)` in core and tested; the window black-box tests remove their temporary homes; the archived `add-cross-window-focus` task 2.1 wording matches the helpers that exist.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- [`ctrl+alt+n` may collide with other extensions on other machines] → a normal VS Code keybinding, rebindable.
- [Users with the view already dragged elsewhere] → VS Code keeps a moved view where the user put it.

# Proposal

## Why

The session view made jumping between sessions easy, so the developer wants it faster still: one click or one key to the session that needs them, a view that stays in the same place in every VS Code window (inside the Explorer it shifts from window to window), and the option to give each worker a full-width tab now that side-by-side placement matters less.

## What Changes

- Clicking the status-bar item focuses the longest-waiting session in any window; with nothing waiting it opens the view.
- A "Toolkit: Next waiting session" command, bound to `Ctrl+Alt+N`, cycles through waiting sessions in urgency order.
- "Claude sessions" moves to its own Activity Bar container with its own icon.
- A setting `claudeToolkit.workerLayout`: `beside` (default, today's layout) or `tabs` (workers open as tabs in the coordinator's editor group).
- Open advisory findings of the cross-window review: registry files are removed by their file name, focus requests are written atomically, the click routing gets tests, the window black-box tests clean their temporary homes, and the archived tasks wording is corrected.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

None.

### Modified Capabilities

- `session-status`: status-bar jump, next-waiting command, Activity Bar placement.
- `vscode-session-launcher`: worker layout setting.

## Impact

`vscode/` (package.json, sessions view, core helpers), tests, README.

# Spec Delta

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Jump to the waiting session

Clicking the status-bar item SHALL focus the most urgent waiting session (longest waiting first), in this or another window as a card click does; with no session waiting it SHALL open the sessions view.

#### Scenario: Sessions waiting

- **WHEN** two sessions wait and the developer clicks the status-bar item
- **THEN** the one waiting longest is focused

#### Scenario: Nothing waiting

- **WHEN** no session waits and the developer clicks the status-bar item
- **THEN** the sessions view opens

### Requirement: Next waiting session

A command "Toolkit: Next waiting session", bound by default to `Ctrl+Alt+N`, SHALL focus the waiting sessions one after another in urgency order, starting again from the first after the last; with none waiting it SHALL show a short message.

#### Scenario: Cycling

- **WHEN** three sessions wait and the developer presses the shortcut three times
- **THEN** each of the three is focused once, in urgency order

### Requirement: Fixed view placement

"Claude sessions" SHALL live in its own Activity Bar container, so it appears in the same place in every window.

#### Scenario: Two windows

- **WHEN** the developer switches between two VS Code windows
- **THEN** both show the "Claude sessions" container under the same Activity Bar icon

### Requirement: Safe registry and focus files

Window registry files SHALL be removed by the name of the file read, including unreadable ones; registry files and focus requests SHALL be written to a temporary file and renamed into place, so a reader never sees a partial file.

#### Scenario: Unreadable registry file

- **WHEN** a window file cannot be parsed
- **THEN** the next reader deletes that file and no other

# Spec Delta

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Worker layout

A machine-scoped setting `claudeToolkit.workerLayout` SHALL choose where worker tabs open: `beside` (default) opens them in the column next to the coordinator, `tabs` opens them as tabs in the coordinator's column.

#### Scenario: Default layout

- **WHEN** the setting is not changed
- **THEN** workers open beside the coordinator, as before

#### Scenario: Tabs layout

- **WHEN** the setting is `tabs` and the coordinator requests a worker
- **THEN** the worker opens as a full-width tab in the coordinator's column without taking focus

# Tasks

## 1. Logic

- [x] 1.1 Add `waitingSessions`, `nextWaiting` and `clickAction` to `vscode/status-core.js`, change `terminalOptions` to take a role and a layout, and verify with tests including wrap-around and an unknown last session

## 2. VS Code

- [x] 2.1 Status-bar command and "Next waiting session" command with `ctrl+alt+n`, Activity Bar container with icon, `claudeToolkit.workerLayout` setting; verify VS Code loads them
- [x] 2.2 Registry deletion by file name, atomic focus requests, black-box temp cleanup, archived wording; verify with tests
- [x] 2.3 Document the shortcut, the status-bar jump, the container and the layout setting in README

## 3. Acceptance

- [x] 3.1 With the developer: status-bar click and shortcut reach waiting sessions in both windows, the container sits in the same place in both windows, and `tabs` layout opens a worker full width

# Tasks

## 1. Hook

- [x] 1.1 Write an `.ended` marker at SessionEnd and record nothing for a session that has one; remove markers with the stale cleanup; verify with hook tests

## 2. Window registry and focus

- [x] 2.1 Add pure helpers (live-window filter, session location, location label, latest session per title) to `vscode/status-core.js` with tests
- [x] 2.2 Publish and remove the window file, watch the window's own focus request, and route clicks to this window, another window or a message in `sessions-view.js`; verify VS Code loads it without errors
- [x] 2.3 Correct the archived proposal wording and document cross-window focus in README

## 3. Acceptance

- [x] 3.1 With the developer and two VS Code windows, click a card held by the other window and verify the window comes to the front with the right tab; click a hand-started session and verify only a message appears
